JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed this petition U/S 22 of The Employees Compensation Act, 1923 for claiming compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest in respect of the injuries sustained by him in the motor vehicle accident on 06.01.2018.

2. The petitioner contended that the 1 st respondent is the R.C. owner of Ashok Leyland 3118 IL Lorry bearing reg.No.KA41B1871 and insured with 2 nd respondent vide Policy No.141521723340012697, valid from 01.11.2017 to 31.10.2018.

That on 06.01.2018 at about 4.30 am while the petitioner was driving the said Ashok Leyland 3118 IL Lorry bearing reg.No.KA41B 1871 travelling on Bangalore to SCCH12 3 ECA.No.81/2019 Mangalore NH75, proceeding towards Sakaleshpura Siradi Ghat, at that time, the driver of the lorry drove the said lorry in a rash and negligent manner with over high speed and suddenly turned the lorry towards right side dig and dashed the front portion due to which the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bangalore wherein, he was admitted as inpatient and received treatment and follow up treatment.
That petitioner has spent huge amount towards medical treatment and hospital charges, conveyance, nourishment, attendant charges etc.
That petitioner was working as a Driver under the 1st respondent and he was aged about 26 years at the time of accident.
He was drawing Rs.13,000/ per month and Rs.500/ bata per day before the accident.
On account of injuries sustained in the accident, he could not attend to work and he incurred loss of earning capacity.
The accident has caused permanent disability, The Sakaleshpura Police have registered a case in Crime No.07/2018 for the offences p/u/s 279,337 of IPC.
On all these grounds he prayed to allow the petition.
3. After registering the case the notices were issued to the respondents no. 1 and 2, they have appeared through their counsel and filed their objections separately.

The respondent no.1 in his written statement has contended that the petition is not maintainable either on law or on facts and contended that the petition is bad for mis joinder and nonjoinder of necessary parties.

That the above petition has to be filed before the Commissioner under SCCH12 4 ECA.No.81/2019 Section 22 of Employees Compensation Act appointed for the purpose under Section 20 of The Act, and this court has no jurisdiction to try the above case.
That the petitioner has not complied with the mandatory provision of the Act by giving notice of accident to the employer.

But in the case on hand the respondent no.1 is not the employer of the petitioner as alleged by him and stated that there is no relationship between the 1st respondent and the petitioner as employer and employee.
That this respondent is the R.C. owner of the Ashok Leyland Lorry 3118 IL bearing reg.no.KA41B1871.
That this respondent has purchased the vehicle in question and he has sold the same to one Anil Kumar K.N on 02.06.2016.
In fact at the time of agreement this respondent has executed all the forms required for the purpose of transfer of R.C into the name of Anil Kumar K.N.

That petitioner has colluded with the said Anil Kumar and filed this false petition Anandaiah Salimath vs Bore Gowda on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142736311/
2 in order to get wrongful gain.

This respondent does not know whether the said vehicle is insured with 2nd respondent as he has sold the vehicle to Anil Kumar K.N on 02.06.2016 for sum of Rs.4,00,000/ with condition that said Anil Kumar has to pay remaining EMIs of Rs.54,000/ per month till the entire loan is completed and also he is entitled to get back the loan documents from Cholamandalam Finance in which all documents are pledged.
That the caseon hand is bad for mis joinder and nonjoinder of necessary party.

That this respondent is no wayway connected with the said accident, copy of FIR and complaint by the said Anil Kumar.K.N clearly indicate that this SCCH12 5 ECA.No.81/2019 respondent is no way concerned to the said accident.
Though the said Anil Kumar K.N has purchased the vehicle in question and necessary documents are provided to him he failed to get registered the vehicle in his name.
The IMV report clearly opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
The date and manner of accident mentioned in the petition are not within the knowledge of this respondent.
Then he again mentioned in the written statement that due to rash and negligent driving of the petitioner while he was in sleepy mode he himself met with the accident due to his own fault.
He suppressed the real facts as he was engaged by Anil Kumar K.N to drive the vehicle in question.
Therefore, this respondent is no way connected with the accident.
There is no employer and employee relationship between this respondent and the petitioner.
As such, Anil Kumar K.N is necessary party to the case.
The age, income and occupation as alleged in the petition are denied On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. The respondent no.2 in his written statement has contended that the petition is not maintainable either on law or on facts.
The age, income and occupation of the petitioner is denied.
The mode of accident and amount spent for medical treatment and other charges are denied.
The loss of income due to disability is denied.
That petitioner has not sent any claim notice to the respondents.
Therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay interest from the date of SCCH12 6 ECA.No.81/2019 accident.

In para 5 of the written statement it is stated that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing reg.No.KA41B1871 and police have falsely implicated the lorry.

As per Section 134 of IMV Act policy details has to be furnished by respondent,
but 1st respondent has not done so.
The mandatory duty under 158(6) of IMV Act is not complied by the police.
The said lorry was not involved in the accident.
The other allegations made in the petition are denied.

That claimant was not having effective driving licence to drive the heavy goods vehicles as such there is gross violation of policy terms and conditions and police in collusion with the owner of the lorry has changed the driver of the lorry.
Therefore, this respondent is not liable to indemnify the owner.
For the delayed period, petitioner is not entitled for interest.
This respondent reserves right to contest the petition under Section 170 if the owner fails to contest the case.
On all these grounds he prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. On application filed by the 1 st respondent under Order 1 Rule 10 of CPC seeking to implead the alleged purchaser of lorry, he appeared through counsel and not filed any objections to I.A.
The said application came to be allowed on 16.12.2020 and he has not filed written statement from his side even after sufficient opportunity being given to him.

Hence, written statement of respondent no.3 is taken as not filed on 24.08.2021 and case is proceed for evidence.

On the basis of the above pleadings, my predecessorsin office have framed the following;
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves the employee and employer relation between him and respondent no.1?

2. Whether the Petitioner proves that on 06.01.2018 at about 4.30 am he was on duty and was driving Lorry bearing reg.No.KA41 B1871 loaded with granite and was proceeding on Bangalore to Mangalore NH 75 and while so proceeding towards Sakaleshpura Siradi Ghat, at that time, the driver of the lorry drove the said lorry with high speed and suddenly turn the lorry towards right side dig and dashed the lorry front portion and caused accident, as a result of which, the petitioner sustained fracture injuries to his both legs and other bodily injuries during the course of employment under respondent no.1?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so to what extent and from whom ?
4. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to prove the above issues the petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1.

Through him Ex.
P1 to 19 documents are marked.
He is fully cross examined by respondent no.2.

On the contrary,
respondent no.1 got examined as R.W.1.
Through him Ex.R.1 to R.9 documents are marked.
The Deputy Legal Manager of 2 nd respondent insurance company got examined as R.W.2.

Through her SCCH12 8 ECA.No.81/2019 Ex.R.10 and 11 documents are marked and closed their side evidence.
8. Heard the arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.
My answers on the above issues are as follows;

ISSUE No.1 : In the Negative,
 ISSUE No. 2 : In the Negative,
 ISSUE No.3 : In the Negative

,
 ISSUE No.4 : As per final order  for the following  REASONS 9. ISSUE NO. 1 : To claim compensation under the Employees Compensation Act petitioner has to prove employer and employee relationship between himself and respondent no.1.
In the present case, in his petition,petitioner contended that, he is employee under respondent no.1.
He stated that he was working as driver under the 1st respondent at the time of accident.
In chief examination also he stated the same.
But, respondent no.1 disputed that he is the employer of petitioner.
In the cross examination of P.W.1 there are several admissions by P.W.1 that there is error in his petition as well as in his chief examination.
He admitted that he was working under one Anil Kumar K.N and the said Anil Kumar has entrusted him with the work.

He has clearly admitted that he was not working Anandaiah Salimath vs Bore Gowda on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142736311/
4 under respondent no.1 and there is no employer and employee relationship between himself and respondent no.1.

The very admissions of the P.W.1, petitioner in his cross examination reads as under:
This goes to show that, the petitioner was working under respondent no.3 and not under respondent no.1.
Therefore, the entire case of the petitioner that he was working under respondent n.1 is not proved.
His pleadings and evidence are contrary to each other.
There are also several errors in the chief examination of P.W.1.
When he was working under Anil Kumar he cannot say that Boregowda is employer of him as stated in the petition.

In view of these admission nothing more is required to decide the case of petitioner that he was not the employer under 1 st respondent and there is no employer and employee relationship between petitioner and respondent no.1.

Hence, without further discussion on the above point this court holds that petitioner has failed to prove issue no.1 in his favour and I Anandaiah Salimath vs Bore Gowda on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142736311/
5 answer this issue in the Negative.
10. ISSUE NO.2: This issue is regarding proof of accident during the course of employment.

sentences.text: It is stated in the petition that on 06.01.2018 about 4.30 am when petitioner was on duty and was driving Lorry bearing reg.No.KA41B1871 loaded with granite and was proceeding on Bangalore to Mangalore NH75 and while so proceeding towards Sakaleshpura Siradi Ghat, at that time, the driver of the lorry drove the said lorry with high speed and suddenly turn the lorry towards right side dig and dashed the lorry front portion and caused accident, as a result of which, the petitioner sustained fracture injuries to his both legs and other bodily injuries during the course of employment under respondent SCCH12 11 ECA.No.81/2019 no.1.
But per his statement in the cross examination he admitted that he was not working under respondent no.1 and he was working as per the instructions of respondent no.3.
Even Ex.R.1 Sale agreement produced by respondent no.1 shows that, vehicle Lorry bearing reg.No.KA41B1871 is sold to 3rd respondent long before the accident on 02.06.2016.
The genuineness or veracity of the said sale agreement is not in question in this case.
As per Ex.P.2 first information given by Anil Kumar respondent no.3, he stated that he appointed petitioner for work and on GPA he had taken lorry from Boregowda i.e., respondent no.1.
When that it is the case, accident has not occurred during the course of employment with respondent no.1.

No doubt,
insurance was valid as on the date of accident.
It was standing in the name of R1 and it is also not changed in the name of R3.
Neither D.L or insurance was changed in the name of R3 though he purchased the vehicle.
Hence without proof of employer and employee relationship as stated in the petition, compensation cannot be awarded under E.C.A to petitioner.
Therefore, petitioner has failed to prove this issue.
Hence, I hold this issue in the Negative.
11. ISSUE NO.3:
In view of the above discussion, Petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the Employees Compensation Act at the hands of respondent no.1.
The pleadings of the petitioner and proof in the present case are contrary to each other.
Therefore, no compensation can be SCCH12 12 ECA.No.81/2019 awarded to petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer this issue in the Negative.
12. ISSUE NO.4:

In view of the above reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 22 of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 is hereby dismissed with cost.
Draw award accordingly.
